area: Mod capability boundary: what a Big Ambitions mod can REGISTER natively vs. what needs bundled Harmony, for a first-class "Store Manager" HQ meta-role
findings:
## 1. The ModAPI surface is tiny. The real integration points are plain `public static` methods on the game assembly.

`BigAmbitions.ModAPI.dll` (decomp/BigAmbitions.ModAPI/BigAmbitions.ModAPI.decompiled.cs, ~1500 lines, 28 types total) contains ONLY: the entry attributes (`RegisterModClassAttribute`, `ModEntryOnCityLoadAttribute`, `ModEntryOnInitializationLoadAttribute`, `ModEntryMainMenuAttribute`, `ModEntryOnIntroLoadAttribute`, `ModEntryOnBlueprintCreatorLoadAttribute`), `ModContext { ModRootPath, ModId, IModLogger Logger }` (no save API, no service locator), `IModBigAmbitions { string[] RelativeAssetBundlePaths; OnLoadAsync(ModContext); OnUnloadAsync() }`, `ModBigAmbitionsBase`, `IModLogger`/`UnityModLogger`, `ModEvents { onModsLoaded, onModsUnloaded }`, `ModEnumHash.GetSafeHash(string)`, `BAModAPI.Services.AssetService` (AssetBundle loader), `ServiceHelper`, `UnityLifecycleProvider` (static `OnUpdate`/`OnLateUpdate`/`OnFixedUpdate` Actions), and the `BigAmbitions.Mods` options builder (`ModOptions`, `OptionsService`, `ButtonOption`/`ToggleOption`/`SliderOption`/`DropdownOption`/`HeaderOption`/`SplitterOption`, plus the extensible abstract `ModOption`).

The only *typed registration API* is `BAModAPI.ModdingAPI` (decomp/BigAmbitions/BAModAPI/ModdingAPI.cs) and it exposes exactly two things:
- `RegisterModBusinessType(BusinessType)` / `UnregisterModBusinessType(...)`
- `RegisterModVehicleType(VehicleType)` / `UnregisterModVehicleType(...)`

There is NO `RegisterModItem`, NO `RegisterModSkill`, NO `RegisterModManager`, NO HQ-plan registration, NO smartphone-app registration.

Everything else a Store Manager mod needs is done by calling the game's own `public static` helpers directly (the mod DLL references `BigAmbitions.dll` + `BAModAPI.dll`; `ModCompatibilityValidator` only checks that referenced game-assembly MAJOR versions match — decomp/ModsInternal/BigAmbitions.ModsInternal/ModCompatibilityValidator.cs). Harmony is NOT blocklisted; `ModAssemblyLoader.TryLoadDependenciesAsync` loads every `*.dll` under the mod's `Dependencies/` folder recursively (ModAssemblyLoader.cs:135-142), so bundling `0Harmony.dll` is a supported pattern.

## 2. Custom SKILL — possible WITHOUT Harmony via `SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded`, but with no persistence hook (must re-inject every load) and some crash risk.

Skill model (decomp/BigAmbitions.Characters/BigAmbitions.Characters.decompiled.cs:603-670):
- `BigAmbitions.Characters.Skills.Skill { string name; float value }` — per-employee, stored in `CharacterData.skills` (List<Skill>), string-keyed. `EmployeeInstance.GetPrimarySkill()` = `characterData.skills.First().name`.
- `SkillData : TaggedScriptableObject` — `[CreateAssetMenu("BigAmbitions/SkillData")]`; public fields `skillName`, `baseHourlyWage`, `trainingCostMultiplier`, `secondarySkill`, `secondarySkillRange`, `icon28` (Sprite), `associatedColorGradient` (Gradient), `possibleDealbreakers` (List<string>).
- `SkillHelper` (static): `public const string AddressableLabel = "Skills"`; private `Dictionary<string,SkillData> Skills`; `public static IEnumerable<string> AllSkillNames => Skills.Keys`; `public static void OnSkillDataLoaded(IList<SkillData>)` (Clears then rebuilds the dict); `public static SkillData GetData(string)` / `GetData(Skill)`.

Loading path (decomp/BigAmbitions/BigAmbitions.SaveSystem/AddressableLoader.cs:170): `Register<SkillData>("Skills", SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded)` inside `RegisterAll()`, driven by `Addressables.LoadAssetsAsync<SkillData>("Skills", null).WaitForCompletion()`. `AddressableLoader.RegisterAndLoadAll()` runs in `SaveGameManager.TryPrepareLoad` (SaveGameManager.cs:339) and the new-game path (:467) — i.e. once per save load / new game, BEFORE the city scene loads and BEFORE `ModLifecycleLoader.LoadScopeAsync(ModActivationScope.City)` runs the mod's `[ModEntryOnCityLoad]`. So a `[ModEntryOnCityLoad]` mod runs after skills are loaded and can append its own.

How a mod injects a skill natively (no Harmony): in `OnLoadAsync`, rebuild the list and call the public method:
```
var list = SkillHelper.AllSkillNames.Select(SkillHelper.GetData).Where(d => d != null).ToList();
var sm = ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData>();
sm.skillName = "storemanager:skill_manager"; sm.baseHourlyWage = 45f; sm.trainingCostMultiplier = 1f;
sm.secondarySkill = ""; sm.associatedColorGradient = new Gradient();
sm.icon28 = SkillHelper.GetData("ba:skill_hrmanager")?.icon28;
sm.possibleDealbreakers = new List<string>();
list.Add(sm); SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded(list);
```

CRITICAL asymmetry vs BusinessType: `BusinessTypeHelper.OnBusinessTypesLoaded` keeps a private `ModBusinessTypes` dict and RE-MERGES mod business types on every reload (decomp/BigAmbitions/Helpers/BusinessTypeHelper.cs:23-50) — a real persistent mod hook. `SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded` has NO such preservation; it Clears and rebuilds purely from Addressables. So a mod skill is wiped on every save-load / scene reload and the mod MUST re-inject it each `[ModEntryOnCityLoad]`.

Why the skill MUST be registered if the manager is ever scheduled or shown: several call sites do `SkillHelper.GetData(name).<field>` with no null guard and will NullReferenceException:
- `EmployeeHelper.CalculateHourlyWageForSkill` (EmployeeHelper.cs:348, 356) — `.baseHourlyWage`
- `EmployeeHelper.GetTrainingCost` (:442) — `.trainingCostMultiplier`
- `RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate` (RecruitmentHelper.cs:65-66) — `.secondarySkill`
- `ScheduleEmployeeInfoBox` (UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.Schedule/ScheduleEmployeeInfoBox.cs:60) — `SkillHelper.GetData(skill).icon28` when the employee is shown in the scheduler
- `ScheduleHelper` (UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.Schedule/ScheduleHelper.cs:118) — `.associatedColorGradient`
- `JobDemandHelper` (:124, :142), `RecruitmentAgencyDialog` (:158), `RecruitmentSettings` (:126) — `.HasTag(...)`

`EmployeeInstance.HasAnySkillWithTag` (EmployeeInstance.cs:230/235) is null-safe in the OTHER direction: `x?.HasTag(tag) ?? true` → an unknown skill is treated as HAVING every queried tag, which is itself a subtle correctness hazard. `EmployeeFilterController`/`CandidateFilterController` DO null-check `GetData` (:14). A registered skill also appears in the Headhunter recruiting dropdown (HeadhuntersRecruitingTab.cs:371), employee/candidate filters, and the uniform editor — mostly benign.

Asset-bundle route for a real Addressable-labelled SkillData: the game never calls `Addressables.LoadContentCatalogAsync` for mods, and `AssetService` uses raw `AssetBundle.LoadFromFile` (not Addressables), so a mod bundle is NOT part of the "Skills" Addressables label. A mod could ship a `SkillData` .asset inside its own AssetBundle and `AssetService.LoadAsset<SkillData>(modId, bundleKey, name)` it, then still has to hand it to `SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded` itself — the bundle only saves you from constructing the ScriptableObject / authoring the Sprite+Gradient. Building such a bundle needs a Unity editor project on the game's exact Unity version referencing the game assemblies.

## 3. Custom HQ MANAGER-PLAN TYPE — NOT possible natively. Needs Harmony on serialization + BizMan UI, or reuse of `modData` + a hand-built UI.

`GameInstance` (decomp/BigAmbitions/GameInstance.cs) is `[Serializable]` with HARD-TYPED plan lists:
- `:218  public List<LogisticsManagerPlan> logisticsManagerPlans`
- `:220  public List<HeadhunterPlan> headhunterPlans`
- `:222  public List<HrManagerPlan> hrManagerPlans`
- `:224  public List<PricingManagerPlan> pricingManagerPlans`
(plus PurchasingAgent is modelled as `ImportPartnership`.)

Each plan type has: its own concrete class in `Buildings.Office.Headquarters.*` (e.g. HrManagerPlan.cs, PricingManagerPlan.cs, LogisticsManagerPlan.cs), its own static `*Helper` (`SaveGameManager.Current.<field>.Where(...)`), its own hourly/daily tick call wired explicitly in `GameManager` (PricingManagerHelper.RunHourly at GameManager.cs:617; HR training via `HRManager.WorkDaily()` reached from `EmployeeHelper.WorkDaily()` at :674), its own compat-fix purge passes (Player.SaveSystem.CompatibilityFixes.*/RemoveInvalidPlans.cs etc.), and its own prefab-backed BizMan UI (`HrManagersPlanList : MonoBehaviour` with `[SerializeField]` prefab refs, HrManagersPlanList.cs).

There is NO registry, NO `List<IManagerPlan>`, NO interface. Adding a genuine 5th plan type requires patching `GameInstance` (new field) + both serializers + wiring a tick + a BizMan tab + a UI prefab. That is a full Harmony + asset-bundle project.

Serialization detail (decomp/BigAmbitions/SaveGameSerializationHelper.cs): JSON = Newtonsoft with `TypeNameHandling.Auto`; binary (.hsg) = OdinSerializer `DataFormat.Binary` with `AllowDeserializeInvalidData = true` and a custom `SaveGameSerializationPolicy`. `TypeNameHandling.Auto` means a mod's `StoreManager : EmployeeInstance` (polymorphic, in `List<EmployeeInstance> EmployeeInstances`) CAN round-trip its `$type` IF the mod assembly is loaded at deserialize time (it is — mod DLLs load at main-menu discovery, before save load, and `AppDomain.AssemblyResolve` is hooked to `ModAssemblyLoader.OnAssemblyResolve`). But: if the mod is later removed, the save carries dangling `$type`s, and the compat-fix framework actively deletes plan/employee references it cannot resolve. Recommendation: do NOT subclass; keep the manager a plain `EmployeeInstance`.

The save-attached persistence hook that DOES exist: `GameInstance.modData` — `decomp/BigAmbitions/GameInstance.cs:248  public Dictionary<string,string> modData = new Dictionary<string,string>();` It is a plain public field (not `[NonSerialized]`), round-trips in both serializers, and is completely unused by the base game (only reference in the whole tree is its declaration). Access via `SaveGameManager.Current.modData`; flush the mod's in-memory state to it on `GlobalEvents.onSaveGame` (fired in `SaveGameManager.Save` before serialize, GlobalEvents.cs:28). This is THE place to persist StoreManagerPlan data (mod id → JSON blob) instead of a side file. `ModContext` has no save methods; there is no `IModSaveData` interface anywhere.

## 4. `enums.txt` / `ModEnumDefinitions` — only defines hashed value names for EXISTING enum types, and is used ONLY for cross-mod collision warnings. It does NOT make new enum values work in the game.

decomp/ModsInternal/BigAmbitions.ModsInternal/ModEnumDefinitions.cs: `TryDefineModEnums(ModInfo)` reads `<modFolder>/enums.txt`, each line `Some.Namespace.EnumType.NewValueName` (assembly defaults to `BigAmbitions`). It resolves the `Type` via `Type.GetType`, hashes the value name with `ModEnumHash.GetSafeHash` (SHA-256 of the string → int, bumped out of the reserved 0..2000 range), and records `(enumType, hash) → owningModKey`. The ONLY consumers are `GetModConflictsList` / `GetAllConflictingModsList`, surfaced as a warning popup (`HGModLoader.CheckConflicts`, `SubscribedModUI.cs:73`). Nothing in the game reads `DefinedEnumValueNames` to resolve a hash back to behaviour.

So the "mod enum" pattern is: the mod computes `(SomeEnum)ModEnumHash.GetSafeHash("mymod:whatever")`, uses that int-valued enum, and `enums.txt` just declares it so two mods don't silently collide on the same hash. Whether the cast VALUE actually does anything depends entirely on whether the game dispatches that enum via dictionary/string lookup with graceful fallback (works) or via a `switch` / prefab-name lookup (fails):
- `AppName`: `FullMenu.SelectApp` calls `appName.ToStringFast()` — and `EnumHelpers.ToStringFast(AppName)` (decomp/BigAmbitions/EnumHelpers.cs:292) is a hard `switch` with `_ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(...)`. Plus apps are prefab children of `appsContainer` looked up by name, and `_appButtons` is a fixed `Dictionary<AppName,...>`. → a new smartphone app is NOT feasible without Harmony + asset bundle + patching `EnumHelpers`.
- `WorkShiftType` (decomp/BigAmbitions/WorkShiftType.cs): only `{ Cleaning, Default }`; assigned by `ScheduleHelper.GetWorkShiftType` (Cleaning-station check, else Default). No need or benefit to a new value.
- `ContactCategoryName` (decomp/BigAmbitions/UI.Smartphone.Apps.Contacts/ContactCategoryName.cs): used via `==` equality and `.GetLocalizeKey()`; category tabs are prefab-driven. A new value can be stored on a `Contact` and compared, but won't get a filter tab. Just reuse `ContactCategoryName.Business` or `.Employees` (as the existing confirmed API does).
- No `ba:skill_storemanager`-style enum exists; skills are strings, so `enums.txt` is irrelevant to the skill question entirely.

## 5. Hiring "through the office like the HR Manager" (target item 2) and the BizMan tab.

BizMan tabs are hard-coded (decomp/BigAmbitions/BizManBusiness.cs:203-253 `SetUpTabs()`): for `ba:businesstype_headquarters` the list is literally `{"Schedule","PricingManagers","LogisticsManagers","PurchasingAgents","HRManagers","Headhunters","Settings"}`. `SetTab` does `menu.Find(tabName)` / `containers.Find(tabName)` — the tab GameObject must pre-exist as a prefab child. Each panel (`HrManagersPlanList`, `PricingManagersPlanList`, ...) is a scene `MonoBehaviour` with `[SerializeField]` prefab references, instantiated from the game's own addressables.

The candidate/assignment filter is hard-coded too: `HrManagersPlanList.UpdateHrManagerDropdownForPlan` (HrManagersPlanList.cs:170) filters `x.HasSkill("ba:skill_hrmanager") && x.IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift()` — literal skill string, and it already requires the manager to be SCHEDULED first (matches target item 4). `RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate` (RecruitmentHelper.cs:43-50) chooses the `EmployeeInstance` subclass by a hard `switch` on skill string (`"ba:skill_hrmanager" => new HRManager()`, etc.; default `=> new EmployeeInstance()`); the subclass's only job is overriding `WorkDaily()`/`UnAssignWork()` to call its plan helper.

So a genuine "Store Managers" HQ tab needs: Harmony postfix on `BizManBusiness.Awake`+`SetUpTabs`+`SetTab` to add the tab string and route it, PLUS a UI panel you instantiate yourself (hand-built uGUI or an asset-bundle prefab), PLUS mod-side plan storage in `modData`. The manager itself can stay a plain `EmployeeInstance` (skill registered per §2) and its daily work can be driven from `GlobalEvents.onNewDay` instead of a `WorkDaily` override, so the `RecruitmentHelper` switch does NOT need patching.

The richest NATIVE (no-Harmony) UI surface is the mod options panel: `ModOptionsViewController.SpawnOption` (decomp/ModsInternal/.../ModOptionsViewController.cs:84-96) — for any `ModOption` whose type is not one of the 6 built-ins, it calls `option.SpawnUi(contentRoot, modId)`, and `ModOption.SpawnUi` is `virtual`. A custom `ModOption` subclass can build arbitrary uGUI (or instantiate an asset-bundle prefab) under `contentRoot`. That panel lives in the pause/settings menu, not the smartphone, so it can't be "through the office" but it can host a full hire/assign/limits UI without Harmony.

## 6. Day-to-day behaviour (target items 6-7): fully native.

`GameManager` hourly loop (GameManager.cs:600-645) and daily loop (:670-689) fire `GlobalEvents.onNewHour` / `onNewDay` (GlobalEvents.cs:16,18). The Store Manager's stocking/staffing logic runs there natively. Everything it needs is public:
- Delivery contracts: `SaveGameManager.Current.DeliveryContracts` (List<DeliveryContract>), `DeliveryContract { enabled, repeatingOrder, nextDeliveryDay, wholesaleAddress, businessAddress, items }`, `DeliveryHelper.CanModifyContract(day)` (confirmed API).
- Scheduling: `reg.scheduleDays[i].AddWorkShift()/RemoveWorkShift()`, `WorkShift{startingHour,endingHour,employeeId,itemInstanceId,type}`, `reg.GetAssignableItems()`, `ScheduleAutoFiller`. Note at HQ, work shifts still bind to a workstation item (`ScheduleHelper.AddWorkShift`, ScheduleHelper.cs:266-295) — the manager needs an office desk workstation at the HQ exactly like HR/Pricing managers.
- Multi-store supervision analog already exists: `LogisticsManagerPlan` (decomp/BigAmbitions/Buildings.Office.Headquarters/LogisticsManagerPlan.cs) has `destinations`, `MaxDestinations`, per-destination config, a dedicated alerts `Contact` ("logistics_alerts", `ContactCategoryName.ImportsAndGoods`), and notification deep-links — a good behavioural template. `PricingManagerPlan.GetSupervisedStores()` filters `SaveGameManager.Current.BuildingRegistrations` by neighbourhood+manageable — same pattern for "assign to N stores".
- Visible feedback (target item 1): `Notifications.Show(NotificationType, key, data, secs, dupId, onClick, ...)` with an `onClick` that can call `InstanceBehavior<UIs>.Instance.fullMenu.bizMan.Open(address, "PricingManagers")` (deep-link to an existing tab, as `PricingManagerPlan.OnClickShowPricingManager` does); `Contact.GetContact(...).SendMessage(new TextMessage(key, data))` for phone messages; `Contact.EnsurePermanentContact(id, category, descKey)` for a dedicated "Store Manager" contact thread.

## 7. `BusinessType`/`VehicleType` registration (the only first-class typed hooks) — not directly what a Store Manager needs.

`ModdingAPI.RegisterModBusinessType` → `BusinessTypeHelper.RegisterModBusinessType` + `BuildingTypeHelper.RegisterModBusinessTypeAvailability`. `BusinessType : TaggedScriptableObject` (decomp/BigAmbitions/BusinessType.cs) carries `businessTypeName`, `suitableBuildingType`, `employeePrimarySkills` (string[]), `uniforms`, products, tags, `simulator` (a `BusinessSimulator` ScriptableObject). Persistent across reloads via the `ModBusinessTypes` re-merge. Relevant only if the mod wanted the Store Manager's "office" to be a new modded business type — not required; the base `ba:businesstype_headquarters` is where manager plans live.

## Load / persistence timing summary
Discovery + mod-DLL load: main-menu, `HGModLoader.InitializeMods` → `ModDiscoveryRegistry.DiscoverAllModsAsync` (loads assemblies, runs `enums.txt`) → `LoadScopeAsync(Initialization)` + `LoadScopeAsync(MainMenu)`. City scope: `LoadScene.LoadGame` → `LoadScopeAsync(ModActivationScope.City)` AFTER `SaveGameManager` has deserialized and after `AddressableLoader.RegisterAndLoadAll()`. `ModsLocal/` folder = `Application.persistentDataPath/ModsLocal` (ModDiscoveryRegistry.cs:46); local mods are always discovered (one `.dll` in the mod root, `Dependencies/` for extra DLLs, `Locales/` for localization, `enums.txt` optional).

modFeasibility:
VERDICT TABLE — [capability] -> [classification]

--- Skill ---
Register a new skill string ("storemanager:skill_manager") so wage calc / training / candidate gen / employee card / scheduler don't NPE
  -> ModAPI-adjacent NATIVE (no Harmony): call SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded(existing + new SkillData) in [ModEntryOnCityLoad] OnLoadAsync, every load. SkillData built via ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData>(). NOT persistent (unlike BusinessType) — must re-inject each city load / scene reload.
New skill via asset bundle as a real Addressables "Skills"-labelled asset
  -> NOT how it works. Game never merges mod content catalogs; AssetService is raw AssetBundle. You can ship the SkillData .asset in a bundle to avoid hand-authoring the Sprite/Gradient, but you STILL must hand it to SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded yourself. => effectively same as the native route + asset bundle for the icon.
New skill via enums.txt / ModEnumDefinitions
  -> N/A. Skills are string-keyed, not an enum. enums.txt does nothing for skills.
Make RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate produce a custom EmployeeInstance subclass for the new skill
  -> NEEDS BUNDLED HARMONY on Helpers.RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate (prefix/transpile the skill switch). AVOIDABLE: keep the manager a plain EmployeeInstance and drive its work from GlobalEvents.onNewDay instead of a WorkDaily override.
New skill shows in recruitment-agency / headhunter / job-board skill pickers
  -> NATIVE side effect once registered (HeadhuntersRecruitingTab iterates SkillHelper.AllSkillNames). Filtering by skill tags (hashoursperweekdemand etc.) is unverified — see open questions.

--- HQ manager-plan type ---
Add a genuine 5th manager-plan type (StoreManagerPlan) to GameInstance
  -> NEEDS BUNDLED HARMONY: GameInstance has hard-typed List<HrManagerPlan>/List<PricingManagerPlan>/… — patching the class + Newtonsoft + OdinSerializer policy. INFEASIBLE cleanly. Use GameInstance.modData (string->JSON) for plan storage instead.
Persist mod plan data attached to the save
  -> NATIVE: SaveGameManager.Current.modData (public Dictionary<string,string>, serialized by both formats, unused by base game). Flush on GlobalEvents.onSaveGame. This is the only save hook; ModContext has none.
Tick the manager plans daily/hourly
  -> NATIVE: subscribe GlobalEvents.onNewDay / onNewHour (no Harmony). GameManager's own manager ticks are hard-wired and cannot be extended, but running alongside them from onNewDay is fine.

--- "Hire through the Office / HQ, like HR Manager" (target item 2) ---
A dedicated "Store Managers" BizMan tab at the HQ with add-plan / assign-manager UI
  -> NEEDS BUNDLED HARMONY on UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan.BizManBusiness (Awake + SetUpTabs + SetTab) to inject the tab string + route it, PLUS a UI panel you instantiate (hand-built uGUI or asset-bundle prefab — the native HrManagersPlanList etc. are [SerializeField]-prefab MonoBehaviours you cannot construct). PLUS plan storage in modData.
Reuse an existing spare manager tab
  -> NOT AVAILABLE — all of Pricing/Logistics/HR/Headhunter/PurchasingAgent slots are in use.
A full hire/assign/limits UI without Harmony
